You are working in a Linux container. The repository checked out at /click is the source of the Python library 'click' (version 8.0.1). Fix one bug in it.

BUG REPORT (from a user):
On Windows, when a program is started with `pythonw.exe` there is no console, so `sys.stdout` and `sys.stderr` are `None`. Calling `click.echo("starting up")` then crashes with:

    AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'

The same crash happens when using `click.progressbar(...)` and `click.echo_via_pager(...)`. Expected behavior: when there is no console/stream attached, the output is simply dropped (no crash).

YOUR JOB:
1. Reproduce the bug. You can simulate the missing stream in a script, e.g. /tmp/repro2.py:

```python
import sys
import click

class FakeOut:
    def write(self, s):
        pass
    def flush(self):
        pass

sys.stdout = None
sys.stderr = None
try:
    click.echo("starting up")
    print("echo OK")
except Exception as e:
    print("echo FAILED:", type(e).__name__, e)
```

Note: `print` will also fail with stdout=None, so write results to a file or use os.write(2, ...) / restore stdout before printing. Also test `click.echo(..., err=True)`, `click.echo_via_pager("x")`, and a progressbar over a small iterable, with both sys.stdout and sys.stderr set to None.
2. Find the root cause in the click source. Look at /click/src/click/utils.py: `echo`, `_default_text_stdout`, `_default_text_stderr`, `_force_correct_text_writer`/`_force_correct_text_stream`, `_is_compat_stream_attr`, `_is_binary_stream`, and the pager helpers; also /click/src/click/_termui_impl.py for the progress bar.
3. Fix it minimally in the source files only. Do NOT modify or delete any existing test file. Do not add new features. Keep the change consistent with click's design (e.g. if the default stdout/stderr helpers can return None when the underlying stream is None, `echo` should return early in that case; make sure the pager and progressbar paths are also safe).
4. IMPORTANT: Before editing, run the full pre-existing test suite and record which tests fail (e.g. `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -40`). Those pre-existing failures are the ONLY ones allowed to fail afterwards. After your edit, run the full suite again and make sure no previously-passing test now fails. If your fix breaks a pre-existing green test, find a different fix.
5. Verify normal behavior is unchanged: `click.echo` to a real stream still writes text and newline; `err=True` still goes to stderr; color handling and `click.echo(..., nl=False)` still work; `click.get_text_stream('stdout')` still works when stdout is a real stream.

REPORT BACK (concise): root cause explanation, exact file and lines changed, the unified diff, reproduction output before and after, verification of the normal cases, and the full test suite pass/fail counts before and after your change.

You are working in a Linux container. The repository checked out at /click is the source of the Python library 'click' (version 8.0.1). Fix one bug in it.

BUG REPORT (from a user):
`click.Path(resolve_path=True)` returns a wrong value when the path is a symlink whose target is a *relative* filename. Example:

```python
import click

@click.command()
@click.option("--p", type=click.Path(resolve_path=True))
def cli(p):
    click.echo(p)
```

```console
$ mkdir -p /tmp/demo && cd /tmp/demo
$ touch real.txt
$ ln -s real.txt link
$ cd /
$ cli --p /tmp/demo/link
/real.txt        # WRONG, expected /tmp/demo/real.txt
```

Absolute symlink targets resolve correctly; only relative ones come out wrong (the relative target is being resolved against the current working directory instead of against the directory containing the link).

YOUR JOB:
1. Reproduce with a script (e.g. /tmp/repro5.py) that creates the symlink setup above and prints `click.Path(resolve_path=True).convert(...)` / invokes a CliRunner command with `--p /tmp/demo/link` from a different cwd. Record observed vs expected.
2. Find the root cause in /click/src/click/types.py, class `Path`, method `convert` (look at how `resolve_path` is implemented, e.g. use of `os.path.realpath`, `os.path.abspath`, `os.readlink`, `os.path.islink`, `os.path.dirname`, and any Windows/`sys.version_info` branch).
3. Fix it minimally in the source files only, so that `resolve_path=True` yields the real absolute path for both relative and absolute symlink targets, including multi-hop symlinks. Do NOT modify or delete any existing test file. Do not add new features.
4. IMPORTANT: Before editing, run the full pre-existing test suite and record which tests fail (e.g. `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -40`). Those pre-existing failures are the ONLY ones allowed to fail afterwards. After your edit, run the full suite again and make sure no previously-passing test now fails. Other subagents are concurrently editing other files (/click/src/click/core.py, decorators.py, utils.py, _compat.py, _termui_impl.py) — do not touch those; only edit /click/src/click/types.py.
5. Verify after the fix: (a) relative symlink target -> correct absolute real path; (b) absolute symlink target -> correct; (c) symlink chain (link -> link2 -> real) -> correct; (d) a normal non-symlink path -> unchanged absolute path; (e) `resolve_path=False` behavior unchanged; (f) `exists=True`/`file_okay`/`dir_okay`/`readable`/`writable` checks still work; (g) Windows branch (if any) is not obviously broken.

REPORT BACK (concise): root cause explanation, exact file and lines changed, the unified diff, reproduction output before and after, results of verification cases (a)-(g), and the full test suite pass/fail counts before and after your change.

BUG REPORT (from a user):
A `click.argument(...)` / `click.option(...)` decorator built once and applied to several commands only works the first time. Example:

```python
import click

class MyArgument(click.Argument):
    pass

my_arg = click.argument("name", cls=MyArgument)

@click.command()
@my_arg
def first(name): ...

@click.command()
@my_arg
def second(name): ...
```

Expected: both `first` and `second` use `MyArgument`. Actual: only `first` does; `second` ends up with a plain `click.Argument`. The same happens with `click.option(..., cls=...)` when the decorator is reused.

YOUR JOB:
1. Reproduce with a small script (e.g. /tmp/repro4.py) that builds the decorator once, applies it to two commands, and prints `type(cmd.params[0])` for each. Also test the same for `click.option` with a custom `cls`.
2. Find the root cause. Look at /click/src/click/decorators.py (`argument`, `option`, `_param_memo`) and how `cls`/`attrs` are threaded through, plus /click/src/click/core.py (`Command.__init__` / `_make_command` / `Argument.__init__` / `Option.__init__`). Something is being mutated or consumed on first use (e.g. `attrs.pop('cls')` / `attrs.setdefault(...)` on a dict shared by the closure, or a shared mutable default).
3. Fix it minimally in the source files only so the decorator is reusable and each application creates a fresh parameter of the requested class. Do NOT modify or delete any existing test file. Do not add new features.
4. IMPORTANT: Before editing, run the full pre-existing test suite and record which tests fail (e.g. `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -40`). Those pre-existing failures are the ONLY ones allowed to fail afterwards. After your edit, run the full suite again and make sure no previously-passing test now fails. Note: another subagent is concurrently editing /click/src/click/core.py for a different bug — do not revert or conflict with unrelated edits there; make your change as small as possible and re-read the file before editing.
5. Verify after the fix: (a) the two-command example above gives MyArgument for both; (b) `click.option('--x', cls=MyOption)` reused twice gives MyOption for both; (c) normal single-use decorators still work (params, defaults, help text, `cls=click.Command`/`cls=click.Group` on `click.command`); (d) decorators applied to a `Command` object directly (e.g. `@click.option(...)` on a Command) still work; (e) `click.argument`/`click.option` with no `cls` still produce `Argument`/`Option`.

REPORT BACK (concise): root cause explanation, exact file and lines changed, the unified diff, reproduction output before and after, results of verification cases (a)-(e), and the full test suite pass/fail counts before and after your change.

BUG REPORT (from a user):
A flag option that uses `flag_value` together with `envvar` returns the raw text of the environment variable instead of the configured flag value:

```python
import click

@click.command()
@click.option("--upper", flag_value="upper", envvar="UPPER")
def cmd(upper):
    click.echo(upper)
```

Running with `UPPER=whatever cmd` prints `whatever`. Expected: the environment variable simply switches the flag on, so the value should be `upper` regardless of the variable's contents (i.e. `UPPER=1 cmd` and `UPPER=whatever cmd` both print `upper`).

YOUR JOB:
1. Reproduce with a small script (e.g. /tmp/repro3.py) using `click.testing.CliRunner` with `env={'UPPER': 'whatever'}` and also with the real environment. Record observed vs expected output.
2. Find the root cause in the click source. Look at /click/src/click/core.py: `Parameter.consume_value`, `Option.consume_value`, `Parameter.value_from_envvar`, `Option.value_from_envvar`, `Option.resolve_envvar_value`, and how `is_flag`/`flag_value`/`is_bool_flag` interact. The raw env var string is currently used as the value for such flags.
3. Fix it minimally in the source files only. Do NOT modify or delete any existing test file. Do not add new features. Keep the change consistent with click's design.
4. IMPORTANT: Before editing, run the full pre-existing test suite and record which tests fail (e.g. `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -40`). Those pre-existing failures are the ONLY ones allowed to fail afterwards. After your edit, run the full suite again and make sure no previously-passing test now fails. In particular, search the tests for `envvar` (grep -rn envvar /click/tests) and make sure boolean-flag-from-envvar behavior (e.g. `--on/--off` or `is_flag=True` with `envvar`, where the env value is converted to a bool like '1'/'0'/'true'/'false') is preserved exactly. If your fix breaks a pre-existing green test, find a different fix.
5. Verify after the fix: (a) `flag_value` flag with envvar set to an arbitrary string -> the flag_value; (b) same with envvar set to '1' -> flag_value; (c) envvar unset -> previous default behavior; (d) envvar set to empty string -> treated as unset (resolve_envvar_value returns None for falsy values); (e) boolean flag (`is_flag=True` or `--on/--off`) with envvar still converts the env string to a bool as before; (f) `flag_value` flag passed on the command line still yields the flag_value; (g) options with `multiple=True`/`nargs` and envvar still split values as before.

REPORT BACK (concise): root cause explanation, exact file and lines changed, the unified diff, reproduction output before and after, results of the verification cases (a)-(g), and the full test suite pass/fail counts before and after your change.

BUG REPORT (from a user):
A boolean flag option declared as required is silently ignored:

```python
import click

@click.command()
@click.option("--on/--off", is_flag=True, required=True)
def cli(on):
    click.echo(on)
```

Running `cli` with NO arguments should stop with an error saying the option is missing (click.MissingParameter, exit code 2, message like "Missing option '--on' / '--off'"). Instead the command runs and prints `False`, so `required=True` appears to be ignored for this flag.

YOUR JOB:
1. Reproduce the bug with a small script (use `python -c` or a temp file outside the repo, e.g. /tmp/repro.py). Note the exact observed behavior and exit code.
2. Find the root cause in the click source (most likely /click/src/click/core.py, look at Option.consume_value, Parameter.consume_value, Parameter.process_value, Parameter.value_is_missing, and how bool flags with secondary opts (--on/--off) are parsed).
3. Fix it minimally in the source files only. Do NOT modify or delete any existing test file. Do not add new features or unrelated refactors.
4. IMPORTANT: Before editing, run the full pre-existing test suite and record which tests fail (e.g. `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -40`, or `python -m pytest -q` if tests live elsewhere; also check setup.cfg/pyproject.toml for the configured test command). Those pre-existing failures are the ONLY ones allowed to fail afterwards. After your edit, run the full suite again and make sure no previously-passing test now fails. If your fix breaks a pre-existing green test, you must find a different fix that does not.
5. Verify these related cases still behave sensibly after the fix: (a) `--on/--off` with required=True and no args -> error; (b) `--on/--off` with required=True and `--on` -> True; (c) `--on/--off` with required=True and `--off` -> False; (d) plain `@click.option('--flag', is_flag=True, required=True)` -> error when omitted; (e) flags with an explicit `default=` still work; (f) `--on/--off` WITHOUT required still defaults to False when omitted.

REPORT BACK (concise): root cause explanation, the exact file and lines changed, the unified diff, reproduction output before and after, the related-case results, and the full test suite pass/fail counts before and after your change.

BUG REPORT (from a user):
A `default_map` that turns a boolean flag on by default is not reflected in the help text:

```python
import click

@click.command()
@click.option("--name/--no-name", is_flag=True, show_default=True)
def foo(name):
    click.echo(name)
```

Running `foo` with `default_map={"foo": {"name": True}}` correctly prints `True`, but `foo --help` still shows `[default: no-name]`. Expected: `[default: name]`, matching the value the flag actually takes. The help text seems to ignore `ctx.default_map` and only look at the flag's own `default` attribute.

YOUR JOB:
1. Reproduce with a small script (e.g. /tmp/repro6.py) using `click.testing.CliRunner`: invoke the command with `--help` and `default_map={"foo": {"name": True}}` (and also with `default_map={"foo": {"name": False}}`), and print the help output. Record observed vs expected.
2. Find the root cause in /click/src/click/core.py, method `Option.get_help_record` (look for the `show_default` / `is_bool_flag and secondary_opts` branch that computes `default_string` from `self.default` instead of the effective default). Also check `Option.get_default` / `Parameter.get_default` which consult `ctx.default_map`.
3. Fix it minimally in the source files only, so the help record uses the effective default (respecting `ctx.default_map`). Do NOT modify or delete any existing test file. Do not add new features. Note other subagents are concurrently editing other parts of /click/src/click/core.py for different bugs — re-read the file right before editing and keep your change as small and local as possible; do not revert unrelated edits.
4. IMPORTANT: Before editing, run the full pre-existing test suite and record which tests fail (e.g. `cd /click && python -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -40`). Those pre-existing failures are the ONLY ones allowed to fail afterwards. After your edit, run the full suite again and make sure no previously-passing test now fails. In particular, keep `tests/test_options.py::test_show_default_boolean_flag_name` and `test_show_default_boolean_flag_value` passing, and check tests mentioning `show_default` and `default_map` (grep -rn 'show_default\|default_map' /click/tests).
5. Verify after the fix: (a) `--name/--no-name` with default_map name=True and show_default -> `[default: name]`; (b) default_map name=False -> `[default: no-name]`; (c) no default_map -> `[default: no-name]` (flag default False); (d) `--name/--no-name` with `default=True` -> `[default: name]`; (e) single-opt bool flag `--cache` with show_default -> `[default: False]`/`[default: True]` as before; (f) non-bool options with show_default and default_map still show the default_map value; (g) `show_default='some string'` still overrides.

REPORT BACK (concise): root cause explanation, exact file and lines changed, the unified diff, reproduction output before and after, results of verification cases (a)-(g), and the full test suite pass/fail counts before and after your change.
